title: Book One · Chapter 51: Seven Circles
story:
Mum draws seven circles on paper. She puts it beside Ronan's breakfast bowl.

He counts them twice.

“Is this homework?”

“Do you know your age next week? Count the circles.”

He looks up. He often thinks about his birthday. Then he gets busy and forgets it for an afternoon. Next Tuesday is his birthday. He counts the circles once more.

“Seven,” he says.

Dad nods. “We may need a longer bed for such an old man.”

“My bed is fine.”

“Good. I didn't bring a longer one to breakfast.”

Ronan laughs. Then he thinks about the saving box.

“Could I have a bike?”

Mum and Dad look at each other. Neither looks surprised.

“Not this birthday,” Mum says.

Ronan looks down at the seven circles. He wanted a birthday bike. His hand stays beside the saving box. He puts his spoon down.

“Even an old one?”

“We need more money put aside first,” Dad says. “I still need regular work. We can save for a bike together. But I cannot name a buying date today.”

Ronan takes a bite of rice. He chews it slowly. His eyes stay on the circles.

“What can we have?”

“Would you like some friends here?” Mum asks. “You could play games one afternoon.” There can be noodles for dinner with the family. She can make something sweet in a pan. It will not be a tall shop cake. “Would you like that?” she asks.

“Can it still be round?”

“It will do its best.”

They make a plan with times. He can ask Leo and Jun to come. Their parents need to agree first. Ronan can ask Bo, too. Does Mei like these games? Ronan does not know. He will ask her. “Would you like to come?” he plans to say.

At school, Mei explains her plan. “I have a family visit that afternoon.” She isn't free. Ronan feels disappointed, but he doesn't ask her to change it.

“I can draw you a card,” she says. “Would you like one?”

“I'd like that.”

“What games can we play?” Leo asks. “We have chalk and stones,” Ronan says. “Jun may bring his paper game.” Leo likes those games. “Will the black cat play?” he asks. “Which team is it on?”

“No. It never listens to the rules.”

At home, Ronan opens the tea box. Three coins still lie on the counting paper. Mum bought the food and other things for home. Last week she had one small coin left. She gave it to Ronan for his box. It waits beside his school book now. He adds it to the box and changes the paper to four.

Four is larger than three. It is not a bicycle.

He asks Dad to show him a used bike one day. He wants to know the price. “Can we just look?” he asks Dad. “We can keep the money.” Dad agrees. They can stop at a bike shop together. They will only look at the prices that day.

Then Ronan helps clear the yard for the birthday games. He looks from the chalk circle to the door. There is clear space between them. Mrs Lan asks them to leave space for her washing basket.

He draws a little party plan. One part is for Mrs Lan's basket. He writes NO GAME HERE beside it. He can prepare this part of his birthday now.

Before bed, he folds the seven-circle paper into his book. He still wants a bike. He also wants Tuesday to come. He opens the paper once more. Seven circles are there. He will have games and noodles on Tuesday. He can save for a bike after his birthday.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：birthday＝生日；saving＝存钱；noodles＝面条；price＝价格。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 生日时希望得到什么？
2. 父母怎样讨论愿望，同时说清现在能做到的事？
